Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
In a previous lesson, we learned that [MATH: \max] and [MATH: \min] return the largest and smallest function values, while [MATH: \arg\max] and [MATH: \arg\min] return the corresponding input values.

Content:
In this lesson, we practice finding [MATH: \max,] [MATH: \arg\max,] [MATH: \min,] and [MATH: \arg\min] from common representations of a function:

Content:
- Tables of values
- Graphs

---

Item 2 — Tutorial: Finding Argmax and Argmin From a Table

Content:
When a table lists input-output pairs [MATH: (x,f(x))] for [MATH: x] in some set [MATH: S,] we can read:

Content:

- [MATH: \arg\max_{x \in S} f(x)] by taking the input value where that largest output occurs.

Content:
When a graph shows the points [MATH: (x,f(x))] for [MATH: x] in a set [MATH: S,] we can find:

Content:
The same idea applies to [MATH: \min] and [MATH: \arg\min,] except we look for the lowest point.
